paper: Arithmetic and harmonic realizations of the Clebsch cubic

integral_boundary.geometric_incidence_comparison: over Z[1/N] for an unspecified nonzero N divisible by 2, 3, and 5
integral_boundary.mod_11_scope: good reduction of the explicit golden fibre and exchanger, not a global integral incidence comparison

claims.statement: The arithmetic orientation cover and the degree-six harmonic realization meet on the integral Clebsch cubic line, with the explicit golden fibre specializing at 11 to the finite sheet bit.
Localization at the square of a nonzero odd element splits the involutive algebra into invariant and odd-generator summands.
Over Q, the ordered-icosahedron incidence extension has equation w^2=5J0 and J0 restricts to 16 sigma3^2 on the Clebsch chart.
The two displayed golden six-arcs form the complete fibre over xyz, and the nonbranch Clebsch cover is the constant golden torsor.
The signed matching cubic restricts to 4 sigma3 over F_11 under an explicit A5-equivariant isomorphism.
The explicit golden-fibre exchanger has good reduction modulo 11 and represents the finite sheet involution T11.
The ten face-axis zonal harmonics embed the 1+4+5 permutation module into H_6, with the Clebsch four-space equal to the Petersen minus-two eigenspace.
The degree-six Gaunt cubic restricts to -784000/1247103 times sigma3 on the Clebsch four-channel.
The Clebsch cubic is the symmetry-resolved four-channel restriction of the standard signed degree-six bond-orientational cubic.

boundaries: ALG-1, HC-3, and PH-1 through PH-3 are presently proved in manuscript-ready form.
The checker validates structure and ledger consistency; it does not certify mathematical truth.
The rational Gaunt scalar has denominator divisible by 11, so HC-3 identifies an integral cubic line rather than a reduced rational normalization.
The harmonic identity has a task-owned exact certificate, independent replay, and primary-source normalization audit.

The abstract quadratic algebra is finite etale over D(10J), but comparison with the geometric incidence model is proved only over Z[1/N] for an unspecified N; no claim that every p other than 2 and 5 is incidence-good is made.

The rational 5-twist is an arithmetic normalization of Hitchin's known degree-two incidence cover, not a new construction of that cover; Dye already proves the square-5 field criterion for Clebsch hexagons.
